subject: grayWolf
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: gray wolf standing alert.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'll aim for a compact but solid module, giving the wolf that Warcraft-style exaggerated look—chunky shoulders, painted fur textures, alert stance, keeping the design wild and bold rather than realistic.

Now I'm working out the skeleton structure: a hips root joint, a spine chain running from hips to chest, a neck chain extending to the head, and a tail chain branching off the hips. I'm planning to sweep the spine chain with a radius function to build the body volume, then skin everything to the joint chains for the rig.

For the limbs, I'm setting up each leg as a three-segment IK chain (shoulder, elbow, wrist) with directional hints so the elbow bends backward and the wrist bends forward, positioning the shoulder and foot target points to get a natural stance and checking the leg lengths comfortably cover the target distance.

Now I'm planning the leg geometry with swept limb chains and paw shapes, plus a mottled gray fur paint with a darker saddle and pale belly using noise-based shading. For the head, I'm sketching out the skull, muzzle, nose, ears, glowing amber eye decals, jaw, and fang details.

I'm working out the ruff and tail tufts with scattered fur cards, then figuring out head orientation using absolute model-space offsets from the head joint position rather than relying on local direction words, assuming roughly zero pitch for simplicity.

Now I'm building the skull as a scaled sphere and the muzzle as a tapered box attached to the head bone, positioning them with the offset helper function, and starting work on the lower jaw joint placement.

Working out ear geometry...

Now I'm figuring out eye placement with a decal on the skull sphere — positioning an almond-shaped amber eye texture with a slit pupil, slanted slightly for a wolfish look, mirrored on both sides near the snout.

Then I'm moving on to body shaping, planning a spine sweep with varying rib radii from hips to chest to give the torso a deep, muscular taper.

I'm also adding chunky shoulder masses and shoulder blade spheres near the spine's upper joints to give the creature that bulky Warcraft-style silhouette.

For the tail, I'm laying out a drooping four-point path from the hips curving down and back, giving it three chain segments named tail1 through tail3, parented to the hips with a tail role.

I'm defining a taper radius function for the tail that narrows toward the tip with rounded caps, and darkening the last segment using color bands shifting from the coat color to a near-black shade near the end. For fur texture, I'm scattering tuft-shaped cards along the neck sweep and tail, keeping the count modest, with a grayish tuft drawing tinted toward the coat color.

Now I'm adding paw details: small forward-facing claw spikes at the toes, sunk slightly at the foot position, with the paw itself modeled as a scaled sphere near the ground.

Then I set up the limb chain to end right at the foot target with a rounded cap covered by the paw, and I write a coat paint function that blends grey tones using noise, darkens the back into a saddle pattern, and lightens the belly.

Continuing the coat shader, I lighten the legs toward a tan color and confirm feet rest flush with the ground plane. I consider adding a glow effect for the eyes using a glow kit import, then move on to defining the head joint in the skeletal chain.

Now I'm plotting the neck path with three points curving up and forward to meet the head, giving the wolf an alert posture. I set up the skull sphere geometry at the head position and begin defining the jaw joint as a child of the head.

Adding fur card scatters now — tufts along the neck sweep, tail, and back ruff filtered by upward-facing normals — before finishing with metadata export.
